To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed and evaluated a novel method for finding attacks on TCP congestion control, and found 8 new attacks.

(1) we found 11 attack strategies against the congestion control implementations of five TCP implementations from 5 operating systems, 3 of which are previously unknown; (2) we designed and implemented a virtualized platform for automated attack discovery in TCP congestion control; and (3) we found that 3 of these 5 implementations are vulnerable to attacks that can increase throughput by up to 100%.
we found 8 new attacks against TCP congestion controls, which we believe have not been reported previously.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How to find vulnerabilities in TCP congestion control implementations?
automated attack discovery in TCP congestion control using a model guided approach.
finding new classes of attacks that are not covered by existing fuzzers, and with finding new attacks that are covered by fuzzers, but that are not detected.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TCP implementation of Windows 8.0 is vulnerable to all of these attacks, and that the Linux kernel 3.10.0 and 3.11.0 are vulnerable to all but 1 attack.
the paper proposes an automated attack discovery technique, which is a combination of fuzzing and model-guided testing.
we have found 8 new classes of attack against 5 TCP implementations, and 3 new classes of attack on 2 implementations that had already been found by other researchers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our method can find attacks that are missed by other automated approaches.
we have developed a novel model-guided approach to find vulnerabilities in TCP congestion control implementations and have found 11 classes, including 8 previously unknown classes of attacks.
we found 8 new attacks, 2 of which have been reported to the respective maintainers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the state machine model of TCP congestion control can be used to find attack strategies that can be automatically mapped to concrete attack actions.
a model based approach to attack discovery can be used to find attacks that would otherwise go undetected.
TCP congestion control is still vulnerable to attacks that can increase or decrease the connection throughput, and the attack surface has not decreased over time.
